### mq-activemq-active-standby-one-active-failover

**Claim.** In an active/standby ActiveMQ broker, usually only one broker instance is active at any time while the other is on standby. If one instance malfunctions or undergoes maintenance, the healthy standby instance becomes active and begins accepting incoming communications.

**Write it as.** `only one of the broker instances is active` · `the healthy standby instance to become active`

**Scope.** Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ active/standby broker; usually.

> "Usually, only one of the broker instances is active at any time, while the other broker instance is on standby. If one of the broker instances malfunctions or undergoes maintenance, it takes Amazon MQ a short while to take the inactive instance out of service. This allows the healthy standby instance to become active and to begin accepting incoming communications."
> — [Deployment options for Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ brokers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/amazon-mq-broker-architecture.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

**Scope.** Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ active/standby broker.

Likewise, Amazon MQ provides two endpoints for each wire-level protocol, but only one endpoint is active in each pair at a time. The -1 and -2 suffixes denote a redundant pair. For wire-level protocol endpoints, you should allow your application to connect to either endpoint by using the Failover Transport."
> — [Deployment options for Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ brokers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/amazon-mq-broker-architecture.html)

**Write it as.** `behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB)` · `broker endpoint remains unchanged`

**Scope.** Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ single-instance broker.

> "A single-instance broker is comprised of one broker in one Availability Zone behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB)."
> — [Deployment options for Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ brokers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/rabbitmq-broker-architecture.html)

> "Using an Network Load Balancer ensures that your Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ broker endpoint remains unchanged if the broker instance is replaced during a maintenance window or because of underlying Amazon EC2 hardware failures."
> — [Deployment options for Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ brokers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/rabbitmq-broker-architecture.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.
